title: An Evening at the Movies
cardDescription: Take a trip to the movie theater with familiar words for tickets, seating, and the experience around the screen.
description: Take a trip to the movie theater with familiar words for tickets, seating, and the experience around the screen.
focus: The clues follow a theater visit from admission to finding a seat. Some answers name places or objects, while others describe a person or an action. The setting supplies the everyday meaning.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue asks for admission, a place, a person, or something used during the visit. Short seating and snack words can help cross longer theater words.
words: Printed or digital proof of admission to a movie
Entrance area where moviegoers gather before entering
Person who helps theater visitors find seats
Passage between rows of theater seats
Line of seats facing a movie screen
Large surface on which a movie is projected
Fabric covering that may hang before a theater screen
Puffed corn snack often sold at a movie theater
Fizzy drink sold at a concession stand
Sweet treat sold in a theater snack box
Movie showing held in the afternoon
Short promotional look at a coming movie
Scheduled starting time of a movie screening
Portion of a paper admission ticket kept after entry
Queue of people waiting to buy tickets
Small enclosed station where tickets may be sold
Way out of a theater auditorium
To allow someone to enter a movie showing
To strike the hands together in applause

answerNotes.AISLE: Aisle names the passage between seats. It sounds like isle, a small island, but the theater setting selects the spelling with an initial a.
answerNotes.MATINEE: A matinee is an afternoon performance or screening. It identifies the time of day rather than the type of film.
answerNotes.PREVIEW: A preview offers a look at something before its full release. A movie trailer is one familiar kind of preview.
answerNotes.STUB: A ticket stub is the part retained after a paper ticket is divided. The clue asks for the remaining portion.
answerNotes.USHER: Usher is a person who guides visitors in this clue. The same word can be a verb meaning to guide someone.
answerNotes.ROW: Row means a line of seats and rhymes with go here. The word has another pronunciation when it means an argument.

title: Behind the Movie Camera
cardDescription: Explore the people, equipment, and simple production words used when a movie scene is filmed.
description: Explore the people, equipment, and simple production words used when a movie scene is filmed.
focus: This puzzle looks behind the screen. Clues identify jobs, objects, and stages of filming through direct descriptions. No knowledge of particular actors or release dates is needed.
solvingTip: Ask whether a clue names a worker, a piece of equipment, or a unit of filming. One clue asks for written material, while another asks for a single recording attempt.
words: Device used to record moving images
Person who guides actors and the filming of scenes
Performer who portrays a character in a movie
Written dialogue and action for a film
Part of a film showing a particular event or situation
One recorded attempt at filming a scene
Built or arranged surroundings used for filming
Object handled or displayed by an actor in a scene
Clothing worn to portray a film character
Cosmetics used to change a performer's appearance
Device used to illuminate a filming area
Long pole that holds a microphone near performers
Optical part of a camera that focuses light
To select and arrange recorded film material
Instruction calling for filming to stop
Group of workers who help make a film
Group of performers in a film
Character or part played by an actor
Audio recorded or added for a movie

answerNotes.TAKE: A take is one recording attempt. Several takes of the same scene may be filmed before an editor selects material.
answerNotes.PROP: Prop is short for property in theatrical use. It names a scene object rather than the performer handling it.
answerNotes.BOOM: Boom names a microphone-supporting pole here. It does not mean a loud explosive noise in this equipment clue.
answerNotes.TRIPOD: A tripod has three legs. The prefix tri- helps identify the support described in the clue.
answerNotes.CAST: The cast consists of performers. The crew includes workers in other production jobs, so the group being described matters.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an instruction to stop a take here. In editing, the same word can describe a change from one shot to another.

title: What Kind of Movie?
cardDescription: Match familiar movie types with the characters, moods, and events that help tell a story.
description: Match familiar movie types with the characters, moods, and events that help tell a story.
focus: The clues combine recognizable film categories with simple story words. A genre describes a type of movie; other answers name a character or an event within one. Some films combine several categories.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a whole movie category or one element of a story. Familiar character and action words can provide crossings for longer genre names.
words: Movie type chiefly intended to make an audience laugh
Movie type centered on serious character conflicts
Movie genre associated with frontier towns and cowboys
Movie type in which songs are a major part of the story
Story centered on solving an unexplained event
Story whose central relationship is a love affair
Movie type designed to create suspense and excitement
Genre featuring imagined worlds or magical events
Animated film often made with drawn or stylized characters
Story type involving an exciting journey or undertaking
Sequence of events forming a movie's story
Central character admired for brave actions
Character who opposes others through harmful actions
Journey undertaken to find or achieve something
Detail that helps solve a story's mystery
Sequence in which one character pursues another
Sound a viewer may make at a funny scene
Piece of music with words performed in a musical
Account of connected events told by a film
Female central character admired for courage

answerNotes.MUSICAL: A musical makes songs central to its storytelling. A film can contain background music without belonging to this genre.
answerNotes.WESTERN: Western names a film genre here. The frontier setting distinguishes it from a simple direction on a map.
answerNotes.MYSTERY: A mystery asks the viewer to work through an unexplained event. A clue is a detail within that larger story.
answerNotes.PLOT: Plot is the arrangement of story events. It does not name a piece of land in this film setting.
answerNotes.QUEST: A quest is a purposeful search or journey. The word names the undertaking rather than the person carrying it out.
answerNotes.CARTOON: Cartoon can name an animated film or a still humorous drawing. The clue specifies the moving-image use.

title: Movie Night at Home
cardDescription: Settle in with a crossword about television controls, a comfortable seat, and familiar movie-night objects.
description: Settle in with a crossword about television controls, a comfortable seat, and familiar movie-night objects.
focus: The clues stay with the home viewing experience. Some answers name controls or actions, while others name a place to rest or something nearby. Ordinary words take their meaning from the living-room setting.
solvingTip: Look for a control, an action, or a household object. Turning sound down and stopping playback temporarily are different operations. Short viewing words can help cross longer comfort items.
words: Handheld device used to control a television
Television service selected by a number or name
On-screen list of programs and viewing times
Small control pressed on a television handset
Setting that controls how loud the television sounds
To silence television audio without stopping the picture
Flat display on which a home movie picture appears
Device that produces a television's sound
Written text displaying spoken words on screen
To stop playback temporarily while keeping one's place
To show a recorded scene again
A filmed story watched on a television or cinema screen
Upholstered living-room seat for several viewers
Soft padded support on a viewing-room seat
Warm covering draped over a seated viewer
Puffed snack served in a bowl during home viewing
Round open container holding a movie-night snack
Small serving of food eaten while watching
Movable room light beside a comfortable chair
To reduce the brightness of a room light

answerNotes.REMOTE: Remote names the handheld controller here. The same word can describe something distant in another context.
answerNotes.VOLUME: Volume is the loudness setting in this clue. It does not mean a book or the amount of space an object occupies.
answerNotes.MUTE: Mute silences audio while the picture can continue. Pause temporarily stops playback, so the two controls have different jobs.
answerNotes.CAPTION: A caption displays speech as written text. It is distinct from a program guide listing titles and times.
answerNotes.REPLAY: Replay combines re-, meaning again, with play. It describes viewing recorded material another time.
answerNotes.DIM: Dim is a verb meaning reduce brightness here. The clue asks for an action rather than the lamp itself.

title: In the Silent Picture House
cardDescription: Visit the world of silent films through familiar words for pictures, gestures, music, and visual comedy.
description: Visit the world of silent films through familiar words for pictures, gestures, music, and visual comedy.
focus: This puzzle focuses on ways early films presented a story. Direct clues describe visual actions, picture units, and accompanying music. The words do not require remembering a particular performer or film title.
solvingTip: Notice whether a clue points to a picture, a gesture, music, or a comic action. Short joke and clothing words can provide crossings for the longer film terms.
words: Describing a film made without synchronized spoken dialogue
Text card used to present words between silent-film scenes
Keyboard instrument often used to accompany a silent screening
Large keyboard instrument associated with some old movie theaters
Music composed or arranged to accompany a film
Spool on which a length of motion-picture film is wound
One still image within a motion-picture sequence
A short visual joke in a comedy scene
To communicate through gestures without speaking
Movement of the hands or body that communicates meaning
Broad physical comedy involving falls or exaggerated actions
Prominent performer featured in a film
Surface used to display a projected silent film
Color paired with white in a familiar film-format phrase
Color paired with black in a familiar film-format description
Comic pursuit shown through moving pictures
Outfit used to establish a silent-film character
Headwear used as part of a comic screen outfit
Walking stick sometimes used as a visual comedy prop
Process of casting a film image onto a surface

answerNotes.SILENT: Silent films lack synchronized spoken dialogue in their original format. Screenings could still include live music or other sound.
answerNotes.TITLE: Text cards between scenes are often called intertitles. The clue uses the shorter word for a card carrying words on screen.
answerNotes.SCORE: Score means accompanying music here. It does not refer to points earned in a game.
answerNotes.REEL: A reel holds a strip of film. A frame is one image on that strip, so the container and picture unit differ.
answerNotes.MIME: Mime is used as a verb for communicating through bodily movement. It does not require spoken dialogue.
answerNotes.SLAPSTICK: Slapstick relies on physical actions for comedy. The word names a comic style rather than a particular actor.
